operation_window: 1943-11-20 planning/repositioning through 1943-12-05 immediate aftermath; tactical landing D-Day 1943-11-24

key_sequence.event: Wasp + Princeton suppress Nauru. Nauru is a real but lower-priority useful base; Japan does not divert Marshall main air to rescue it. Separate Japanese reconnaissance confirms another US carrier-cover group, establishing multi-TG invasion scale before D-Day.

Japanese land-based torpedo strike (~22 launched, ~7-9 effective releases) hits USS Independence (CVL-22) with one aerial torpedo. Independence survives but is campaign-out. Japanese loss center ~14 aircraft.

Makin landing begins in morning; Liscome Bay survives because D-Day alert/screen geometry differs from historical D+4 loss conditions. Tarawa landing is delayed into afternoon high-water window with measured-lane LVT/LCVP plan.
Limited Japanese daytime raid disrupts final support synchronization; LVT first waves encounter concentrated surviving beach fire. Later LCVP/LCM use verified lanes as tide rises.

Japanese organized 380-480-man counterattack with 4-5 serviceable Type 95 tanks gains local ground and temporarily disrupts the Red 2/3 connection, but fails to break the beachhead against 6-8 operational M4A2s, artillery, illumination and destroyer fire. Two to four other surviving Type 95s continue as short-hop mobile firepoints into 11/25-26; later action reverts to infiltration.

Major two-way carrier battle. Japanese four-carrier first strike (~160-165) mission-kills Lexington and temporarily damages Yorktown; US counterstrike mission-kills Soryu. Corrected event-local Kinsei Zero component ~20 aircraft is included.
Four-destroyer IJN stand-off Type 93 raid after staggered night-air cueing sinks USS Franks (DD-554); Fujinami takes light-moderate 5-inch damage but withdraws.
Makin organized resistance ends. I-175 torpedoes USS Pierce (APA-50), which survives but is campaign-out; I-175 is damaged by ASW and withdraws.

Tarawa organized resistance continues through the evening after the land-vehicle/hardware rollback. Final coherent pockets collapse overnight; island secure declaration shifts to 11/29 morning. US still secures the Gilberts.

Historical mass Kwajalein/Roi raid is not auto-inherited. US conducts a more limited outer-Marshalls raid/recon while maintaining a large cover reserve against surviving Japanese fleet carriers; no centered major carrier hit.

territory.Tarawa: US-held from 1943-11-29 after organized resistance ends overnight 11/28-29
territory.Makin: US-held from 1943-11-27 after organized resistance ends
territory.Nauru: Japanese-held; runway/air function heavily suppressed 11/23, limited night-staging capability partly restored by early December

US_naval.Independence_CVL22: one aerial torpedo 1943-11-23; campaign-out/long repair; survives
US_naval.Lexington_CV16: one aerial torpedo + 1-2 bomb hits 1943-11-26; campaign mission-kill; survives; major repair
US_naval.Yorktown_CV10: one bomb/near-miss damage 1943-11-26; temporary deck impairment; limited ops next day, near-normal by ~11/29
US_naval.Franks_DD554: sunk/abandoned after one Type 93 hit during 1943-11-26/27 Makin outer-screen raid
US_naval.postbattle_note: Carrier aircraft/orphan groups cross-deck and ferry to surviving carriers/land bases; US replacement and pilot-recovery depth remains superior.
US_naval.fighter_microcombat_note: F6F-3/CIC remains systemically favored; current Kinsei mix causes only small quantitative shift in fighter losses.

Japan_naval.Soryu: two bomb hits flight deck/hangar; mission-kill but propulsion largely intact; withdraws for Truk emergency repair then Japan
Japan_naval.secondary_carriers: Junyo/Hiyo/Ryujo/Zuiho centered Bengal commitment 0 and retained as Pacific/rear-deck reserve; used after battle as cross-deck/ferry/regeneration shock absorbers rather than first-strike fifth/sixth fleet carriers.

night_surface_group.mission: conditional Makin stand-off Type 93 raid; no prolonged gun battle

Japan_naval.Naka_Isuzu: arrive Kwajalein with reinforcement role; no suicidal Tarawa run; personnel/cargo reallocated to Marshall defense after landing outcome becomes clear
Japan_naval.CruDiv7_heavy_group: Chokai/Suzuya/Kumano and associated cover remain reserve; no daylight-suicidal penetration into US carrier/CVE air umbrella
Japan_naval.I175: conducts 11/24 approach without historical Liscome Bay kill; later 11/27 torpedoes Pierce, suffers heavy depth-charge damage but escapes/withdraws
Japan_naval.aircrew_note: Losses are disproportionately painful in strike leaders, torpedo navigators and experienced multi-seat crews; nominal carrier-capable aircraft depth remains far thicker than historical late-1943 Japan.
Japan_naval.fighter_microcombat_note: 13/48 Kinsei in first-strike escort saves about one fighter versus all-Zuisei in longer mission-window diagnostic; 7/52 CAP saves less than one. Route/hit states unchanged.

Tarawa_ground.rule: Construction/air-ground/labor/support personnel are not converted one-for-one into first-line SNLF infantry.

vehicle_OOB_and_serviceability.note: The 11/24 higher-water measured-lane plan avoids the historical wholesale reef delivery failure, but shell holes, seawall passages and surviving 75/37mm fire still remove several tanks. No extra US or Japanese hulls are created.

Tarawa_ground.causal_note: Initial landing remains harsh. The v047 correction restores the 14-Type-95 physical OOB, Branch running-gear/service variants, lower atoll-specific reappearance band, engineer-vehicle uptime and mature registered-fire/ammunition/comms hardware. The 11/24 tide/lane plan still permits much better later-wave US logistics and materially more M4A2s ashore than historical 11/20, so the result is a bounded casualty/timing increase rather than beachhead failure.
Tarawa_ground.organized_resistance_end: 1943-11-29 morning centered; 11/28 evening to 11/29 noon band
Tarawa_ground.rollback_scope: Tarawa ground node reopened to pre-landing 1943-11-24. Naval, carrier-air, submarine and territory-choice nodes were dependency-checked and retained.

Makin_ground.note: Do not scale Tarawa defender quality/fortification directly onto Makin.

immediate_aftermath.US: Strategic victory in Gilberts but fast-carrier price is substantially higher. Avoid deep immediate pursuit; keep carrier cover split and conduct limited outer-Marshall pressure rather than historical mass 12/4 Kwajalein strike.
immediate_aftermath.Japan: Fails to hold Gilberts but preserves three operational first-line carriers, Soryu hull, secondary carrier depth and a still-material Marshall air network. Uses fleet-in-being, dispersed bases, small night raids and submarines rather than repeated all-out strikes.
